items.title: Finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification and control data
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite smooth algebraic frontier stratifications ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.
items.strategy: Every clause is a definition with its well-definedness comments; no existence of stratifications, tubes, controlled lifts or triangulations is asserted. (i) Whitney (a),(b) are stated in the standard Euclidean coordinates of chosen local affine embeddings into $\mathbb C^N$ (the affine-model convention of [[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); the earlier analytic-topology/smoothness Definition supplies analytic topology and intrinsic regularity, not an analytic-chart comparison theorem for the strata; limits are taken in finite-dimensional Grassmannians, and coordinate independence is explicitly not claimed, so no invariant is presupposed. (ii) Tube control data impose smoothness on strata of the ambient stratified space and require compositions only where defined; shrinking is allowed, and local properness is stated as a compactness condition on closed radius ranges. (iii) Compatibility with a stratified submersion $f$ and the three differential equations for a controlled lift are conditions on a given field, not existence claims; local boundedness is flagged as an extra hypothesis. (iv) The conical product convention separates the homeomorphism statement from coefficient transport. (v) The triangulation convention is the deleted-boundary convention of noncompact finite type. All clauses are choice-free: nothing is selected, and the cited published definitions are choice-free.
items.axiom_use: None: a definitional contract; the cited definitions are choice-free and no selection is made.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Section 8 (stratifications, Whitney conditions, links, control data and triangulation)

items.title: Complex algebraic boundary points admit normalized curve arcs
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $V$ be an irreducible complex algebraic variety of positive dimension, let $O\subseteq V$ be a nonempty Zariski open subset and let $z\in V$. There is an irreducible algebraic curve $C\subseteq V$ through $z$ not contained in $V\setminus O$. There is also a holomorphic map $\gamma:\Delta\to V$ from a sufficiently small complex disk with $\gamma(0)=z$ and $\gamma(s)\in O$ for all $s\ne0$. The arc can be obtained by analytically parametrizing a point over $z$ in the finite normalization of $C$.
items.strategy: (1) On an affine chart $V_0$ of $z$, Noether normalisation gives a finite onto morphism $h:V_0\to\mathbb A^d$ and fibre dimension is controlled by dimension theory ([[cor-noether-normalisation-module-finiteness]], [[thm-finite-morphism-integral-closed]], [[thm-lying-over]], [[thm-dimension-formula-for-affine-domains]], [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]]): the proper closed image $h(B)$ of $B=V_0\setminus O$ has dimension $<d$ by [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]]. (2) Choose an affine line through $h(z)$ not contained in $h(B)$: a nonzero polynomial vanishing on $h(B)$ cannot vanish on every line, by the finite-root bound for one-variable polynomials over $\mathbb C$. (3) The inverse image of that line is cut out by $d-1$ equations, so by Krull height every component has dimension exactly one ([[thm-krull-height-theorem]]); a component through $z$ is an irreducible curve not contained in $B$. (4) Normalize the reduced curve ([[thm-normalization-reduced-curve-exists-finite]]), which is regular hence smooth over $\mathbb C$ ([[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]]), and use a holomorphic disk chart at a point over $z$ ([[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]]); since $C\setminus O$ is finite, shrinking the chart makes the punctured arc lie in $O$. AC is inherited from the normalisation and fibre-dimension suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the Noether-normalisation, fibre-dimension, curve-normalisation and perfect-field suppliers cited above; the selection of the line and of the disk chart is finite/algebraic. No other choice principle is used.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry (v6.10), normal varieties, finiteness of integral closure and normalisation of curves (Chapter 8a-8b)

items.title: Generic complex algebraic Whitney regularity
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $S,Y\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be disjoint irreducible smooth locally closed complex algebraic varieties with $Y\subseteq\overline S$ and $\dim Y<\dim S$. There is a proper closed algebraic subset $E\subsetneq Y$ such that $(S,Y)$ satisfies Whitney (a) and (b) at every point of $Y\setminus E$. Finitely many prescribed incident upper strata can be treated with one common exceptional subset by taking a finite union. The same result holds in the affine charts of a quasi-projective algebraic ambient manifold.
items.strategy: Form the graph $G$ of $(x,y)\mapsto(T_xS,[x-y])$ in $\overline S\times Y\times\operatorname{Gr}(\dim S,n)\times\mathbb P^{n-1}$; tangents are Jacobian kernels and Grassmannian charts are algebraic ([[thm-zariski-tangent-space-jacobian-kernel]], [[lem-grassmannian-standard-affine-charts]]), so its reduced closure $Z$ is an irreducible algebraic correspondence over $Y$. Generic fibre purity of the projection $Z\to Y$ ([[thm-generic-fibre-dimension]]) gives a dense open $Y^0$ on which the fibres are pure of dimension $\dim Z-\dim Y$, strictly larger than the generic fibre dimension of the proper closed complement $B=Z\setminus G$, using Noetherian finiteness and dimension drop ([[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]]). At $y\in Y^0$, any limiting incidence point is reached by a normalised holomorphic arc with second coordinate constantly $y$ and punctured part in $G$ ([[lem-complex-algebraic-boundary-points-admit-normalized-curve-arcs]]); writing $x(s)-y=s^mv(s)$ with $v(0)\ne0$ and differentiating covector fields annihilating the tangent planes yields $m\,p_0v(0)=0$ for every annihilator $p_0$ of the limiting plane $T$, hence the limiting secant direction lies in $T$. This proves Whitney (b) for moving lower points, and Whitney (a) follows by inserting intermediate points $y_j=y+\epsilon_jw+o(\epsilon_j)$ along the lower tangent. Finitely many upper strata and affine charts are intersected into one proper exceptional set. AC is inherited from the algebraic fibre and curve suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from [[thm-generic-fibre-dimension]], [[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-boundary-points-admit-normalized-curve-arcs]]. The construction itself selects no infinite family.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Section 8.1-8.2 (Whitney conditions and algebraic Whitney stratifications)

items.title: Complex algebraic morphisms admit compatible finite smooth stratifications
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced separated complex algebraic varieties of finite type, and prescribe finitely many closed algebraic subsets of each. There are finite partitions of $X$ and $Y$ into irreducible smooth locally closed algebraic strata such that every prescribed subset is a union of strata, every stratum closure is a union of strata of no larger dimension with boundary of strictly smaller dimension, and each source stratum maps surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. On analytic spaces each such restriction is a submersion. The source may be empty. No Whitney condition, conical control or topological triviality is asserted.
items.strategy: (1) Round-wise construction on a closed residual subvariety: on each irreducible component remove the nonsmooth locus, the intersections with other components and every prescribed closed subset not containing the component, obtaining a dense smooth open whose closure is the component; the complement loses dimension, and iterating over finitely many components terminates ([[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]], [[thm-nonempty-regular-locus-reduced-variety-perfect-field]], [[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]]) — this gives finite smooth frontier partitions respecting prescribed closed sets. (2) Source and target simultaneously by decreasing target residual dimension: after partitioning the source over the current closed target residual, shrink each target component to a dense open over which every source stratum maps smoothly and onto it ([[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]]), remove it, add emitted closures to the prescription lists and repeat until the target residual is exhausted. (3) Smooth complex strata are analytic manifolds and the restrictions are holomorphic submersions by the Jacobian criterion ([[lem-smooth-map-tangent-surjectivity-criterion]], [[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]]). AC is inherited through the cited algebraic suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through [[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]], [[thm-nonempty-regular-locus-reduced-variety-perfect-field]], [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]] and [[lem-smooth-map-tangent-surjectivity-criterion]]. The finite round induction itself makes no infinite selection.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Theorem 8.10 (algebraic Whitney stratifications and stratified maps)

items.title: Complex algebraic varieties and maps admit compatible finite stratifications
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$ respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is asserted proper.
items.strategy: (1) Replace each prescribed locally closed subset by the two closed subsets $\overline A$ and $\overline A\setminus A$, then construct a Whitney partition of any closed residual variety compatible with a finite closed-set list and with fixed external upper strata: at each round take dense smooth opens of components ([[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]], [[thm-nonempty-regular-locus-reduced-variety-perfect-field]], [[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]]) and remove the generic-exceptional points to obtain Whitney (a),(b) compatibility with every incident earlier upper stratum ([[lem-generic-complex-algebraic-whitney-regularity]]); recurse on the dimension-dropping closed complement. (2) Interleave the smooth map-compatible construction of [[lem-complex-algebraic-morphisms-admit-compatible-finite-smooth-stratifications]] with the Whitney construction by decreasing target residual dimension, shrinking target components to dense opens on which each new source stratum is smooth and onto ([[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]]) and retaining Whitney regularity by restriction. (3) Analytic smoothness and submersivity follow from holomorphic implicit-function charts ([[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]]); analytic properness of the whole restriction over a target stratum follows from compactness of closed bounded sets, continuity and finite products ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]], [[thm-compactness-under-continuous-maps]], [[thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces]]), and projective maps factor through a closed embedding into $Y\times\mathbb P^N$ with $\mathbb P^N$ a continuous image of the unit sphere. AC is inherited from the geometric suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The statement asserts no tube control, isotopy or triangulation.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the algebraic stratification suppliers, [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]] and the compactness suppliers where relevant. No further choice is made in the finite round inductions.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Theorem 8.10 (Whitney stratifications of algebraic varieties; stratified maps)

items.title: Whitney normal tubes have submersive radius and bounded stratumwise lifts
items.statement: Assume AC. Let a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) stratification be embedded in $\mathbb R^N$, let $R$ be one stratum, and choose its ordinary Euclidean normal tube with projection $\pi$ and distance $r(x)=\|x-\pi(x)\|$. Near every point of $R$, after shrinking the tube, the pair $(\pi,r)$ is a submersion on each incident upper stratum. There are smooth stratumwise right inverses for its differential whose norms are locally uniformly bounded near $R$. Consequently a smooth bounded field $w$ on $R$ has smooth locally bounded lifts on each incident stratum with $d\pi(V)=w\circ\pi$ and $dr(V)=0$; there are also radial lifts with $d\pi(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=0$, $dr(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=r$ and $\|V_{\mathrm{rad}}\|\le Cr$. These are lifts relative to this one lower stratum only; no simultaneous Mather control identities or continuous stratified flow is claimed.
items.strategy: In the Euclidean tube write $x=y+n$ with $y=\pi(x)$, $n\perp T_yR$ and $r=\|n\|$, so that $dr(v)=\langle n/r,v\rangle$. For a point $x$ in an incident stratum $S$ consider the matrix $A_x$ of $(d\pi_x,dr_x)$ in a smooth lower-frame; if the lower singular value of $A_x$ failed to be locally bounded below, a contrary sequence would converge to a limiting upper plane $T$ and unit normal direction $u$ with $u\perp T_yR$; Whitney (a) puts $T_yR\subseteq T$ and Whitney (b) puts the radial limit $u$ in $T$ ([[def-finite-complex-algebraic-whitney-stratification-and-control-data]]), so $\|A^*(a,b)\|=\|P_T(a+bu)\|=1$ cannot tend to zero. This uniform bound makes $(\pi,r)$ submersive on every incident upper stratum and makes the explicit right inverse $H_x=A_x^*(A_xA_x^*)^{-1}$ smooth with locally bounded norm, giving the claimed horizontal and radial lifts; the tube and its normal coordinates are supplied by [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]], whose countable-choice hypothesis is met by the declared AC through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Lifts of different strata are not glued, so no simultaneous compatibility is asserted.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through the chain AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]), which supplies the countable-choice hypothesis of the Euclidean tubular neighbourhood theorem [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. The singular-value argument and the lifts are otherwise explicit.

references.title: John Mather, Notes on Topological Stability (1970), Sections 1-2 (Whitney conditions a and b) and 6 (tubular neighbourhoods)

items.title: Relative tubular neighborhoods preserve a chain of submersions
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $S\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ be an embedded smooth manifold and let $F_i:U_i\to B_i$ be a finite family of smooth submersions such that $F_i|_{S\cap U_i}$ is a submersion. Prescribe closed subsets $C_i\subseteq S\cap U_i$, closed relative to $S$. Suppose the maps relevant at each $s\in S$ form a chain: on a neighbourhood of $s$, every $F_i$ with $s\in C_i$ factors smoothly through a single maximal such map $F_j$. Then a tubular retraction $\pi:T\to S$ can be chosen so that $F_i(x)=F_i(\pi(x))$ whenever $\pi(x)\in C_i$ and $x$ lies sufficiently close to its zero-section point in the chosen tube. Its tube map is a smooth embedding from a variable-radius neighbourhood of the normal quotient bundle. Additional prescribed positive pointwise size bounds can be imposed on its displacement and fibre radius. No convex average of manifold-valued retractions is used.
items.strategy: At each $s$ choose adapted coordinates $(b,u,z)$ with $S=\{z=0\}$ and the maximal active map $F_j=b$, straightening $S$ and applying the constant-rank normal form to the restricted submersion ([[thm-constant-rank-theorem-for-manifolds]]); the vertical quotient $Q=T\mathbb R^N|_S/TS$ receives a smooth splitting whose image is vertical for every active $F_i$. Patch the local vertical fields with a locally finite smooth partition subordinate to the local chain neighbourhoods ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]) to obtain a field $W(s,v;x)$ linear in $v$ with $W(s,v;s)=j_s(v)$ whose quotient is $v$ and which is vertical for every active constraint near $x=s$; the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition and of the Euclidean tube theorem are met by the declared AC through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. The time-one endpoint $E(s,v)$ is smooth with $E(s,0)=s$ and $d_vE(s,0)=j_s$, hence a local diffeomorphism by [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]; on the zero section its differential is the tubular splitting. A Lipschitz injectivity-radius argument and a smooth minorant of the resulting positive local bounds (again [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]) make $E$ an injective local diffeomorphism onto a tube, and the constraints give $F_i(E(s,v))=F_i(s)$ wherever the active chain applies. All radius requirements are positive local requirements on $S$, and prescribed size bounds can be enforced by shrinking the minorant.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition-of-unity theorem [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] and the Euclidean tubular neighbourhood theorem [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The ODE and constant-rank arguments are choice-free.

references.title: John Mather, Notes on Topological Stability (1970), Section 7 (control data: existence and relative construction)

items.title: Whitney stratifications admit compatible control data
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ have a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) frontier stratification by locally closed embedded strata. There are tube control data $(T_S,\pi_S,\rho_S)$, with $\rho_S$ a squared bundle radius, such that incident overlap compositions are defined and satisfy $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$, $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$. Incomparable strata have disjoint tubes, $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is a submersion on incident upper strata, and the tube data have local properness over compact lower-stratum slices. If a smooth ambient map $f$ is a submersion on every stratum, the tubes can additionally satisfy $f\pi_S=f$. The statement is about compatible data; continuous controlled flows are a separate construction.
items.strategy: Induct on stratum dimension, retaining outer tubes while shrinking final domains, and impose displacement bounds by $\frac13$ of the distance to the frontier and to incomparable closures ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] gives smooth positive minorants of the resulting local bounds). The displacement bound forces convergent tube points based near the frontier to share their frontier limit, and the incomparable bound makes incomparable tubes disjoint, so active lower controllers always form a chain. Near a new stratum $S$ use inner/middle/outer variable radius bands: the closure of the middle band intersected with $S$ is relatively closed, the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is submersive on $S$ by [[lem-whitney-normal-tubes-have-submersive-radius-and-bounded-stratumwise-lifts]], and lower controllers factor through the maximal active one, so [[lem-relative-tubular-neighborhoods-preserve-a-chain-of-submersions]] applies to produce a tube preserving all active $F_R=(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ (and a given stratified submersion $f$, adjoined as a root controller). Explicit support functions supported on the middle bands and positive on the inner closures, together with the displacement bound, ensure every point of the new tube in an inner band has its base in the compatibility domain; then restrict old tubes to their inner bands and rescale. Comparing the constructed tube with an ordinary Euclidean tube by a smooth ambient diffeomorphism ([[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]) and applying the previous submersion statement makes $(\pi_S,\rho_S)$ submersive on incident upper strata; Whitney (a),(b) are preserved by smooth ambient diffeomorphisms. Local properness is explicit in the bundle model over compact base slices. AC meets the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition and tube suppliers through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]].
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] and [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The induction, band and diffeomorphism arguments are otherwise explicit.

references.title: John Mather, Notes on Topological Stability (1970), Sections 5-7 (Whitney pre-stratifications, tubular neighbourhoods and control data)
Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Section 8.7 (existence of control data)

items.title: Controlled stratified submersions have continuous local trivializations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W$ be a locally closed finite Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth ambient manifold, and let $f:W\to B$ be the restriction of a smooth ambient map that is a submersion on every stratum. Every smooth base field admits, after tube shrinking, a stratumwise smooth locally bounded controlled lift. Its stratumwise ODE solutions form a jointly continuous stratum-preserving local flow with jointly continuous inverse. Each source point has a stratum-preserving product neighbourhood over a small coordinate box in $B$. If $f$ is proper, every base point has a whole-fibre stratum-preserving bundle trivialization. No global simplicial model of $f$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Construct lifts in increasing stratum dimension over the compatible tubes of [[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]]: on a stratum use the minimum-norm right inverse of $(d\pi_R,dr_R)|_{TS}$ supplied by [[lem-whitney-normal-tubes-have-submersive-radius-and-bounded-stratumwise-lifts]] (or of $df$ where no lower controller is active), which lifts the given smooth field because $f\pi_R=f$ and respects the lower controls by the chain factorization. The minimum-norm solutions are locally bounded by a limiting surjectivity argument; patch the finitely many active controllers with a subordinate partition and inner bands, so that only linear equations in the field are summed ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]; its countable-choice hypothesis is met via [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Stratumwise ODE solutions exist and depend smoothly on parameters ([[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]); boundedness plus the compact tube slice and the radius-monotonicity argument exclude finite-time escape to lower strata, giving a common short flow interval for nearby points of possibly different strata, and the compact-slice estimates give joint continuity and a jointly continuous inverse. Ordered coordinate flows then produce stratum-preserving product neighbourhoods, and when $f$ is proper the compact inverse images bound the fields so the construction globalizes to a whole-fibre bundle trivialization.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for the partition-of-unity supplier [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the inherited tube construction. The ODE and compactness arguments are otherwise explicit.

references.title: John Mather, Notes on Topological Stability (1970), Sections 9-11 (controlled vector fields, parameter groups and the isotopy lemmas)

items.title: Algebraic Whitney strata have controlled local conical neighborhoods
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety with a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification. Its analytic stratified space admits compatible tube control data. At every point $y$ of a stratum $R$ there is a stratum-preserving neighbourhood homeomorphism
$$U_y\cong B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c_{<1}(L_y),$$
where $L_y$ is a compact finitely Whitney-stratified real semialgebraic normal link. The ball times cone apex is $R\cap U_y$, and upper strata correspond to their link strata times positive radius and the ball. The local construction can preserve a chosen ordinary normal projection and radius at $R$. Links are locally constant in stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. Proper stratified algebraic submersions, with their actual analytic properness, have whole-fibre local stratified bundle trivializations; local submersions have source-neighbourhood products. No compatible triangulation or finite sheaf-cochain model is assumed or asserted here.
items.strategy: Work in an affine chart about $y$ with only $R$ and its incident upper strata present, and start the compatible tube induction of [[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]] from an ordinary Euclidean tube at $R$ ([[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]], with AC meeting its countable-choice hypothesis through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which by [[lem-whitney-normal-tubes-have-submersive-radius-and-bounded-stratumwise-lifts]] is submersive on all remaining upper strata over a compact base ball. The restriction $g=(\pi,r)$ of the punctured tube to $B\times(0,\epsilon)$ is a proper stratified submersion; the reference fibre $L_y$ is compact and real semialgebraic as the intersection of $X$ with an affine normal plane and a sphere. Lifting base coordinate fields and the radial field with controlled lifts and integrating gives stratum-preserving flows ([[lem-controlled-stratified-submersions-have-continuous-local-trivializations]]); combining horizontal transport at the reference radius with radial transport gives a stratum-preserving homeomorphism $B\times L_y\times(0,r_0)\to X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{0<r<r_0\}$, and adjoining the apex by continuity (uniform normal-radius convergence) yields the cone product. Link strata are smooth by the submersion property and inherit the frontier and Whitney conditions by restricting the control data; horizontal transport identifies them locally constantly along $R$. Properness of a stratified algebraic submersion is the actual analytic properness supplied by [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], and local source products and whole-fibre trivializations then follow from the flow construction.

The properness input is the analytic properness proved in [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]].

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit commuting radial collars
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact finite smooth Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth Euclidean ambient space, with the frontier condition. After shrinking compatible tube data and smoothly rescaling their squared radii by positive functions of their base projections, there are normalized tubes $T_X=\{\rho_X<1\}$ and stratum-preserving radial projections $R_X(s):T_X\setminus X\to\{\rho_X=s\}$ for $0<s<1$. On every incident overlap $Y<X$ they satisfy
$$R_X(s)R_Y(t)=R_Y(t)R_X(s),\qquad \rho_YR_X(s)=\rho_Y,\qquad \rho_XR_Y(t)=\rho_X,$$
whenever the source and target points lie in the indicated retained tubes. They also satisfy $\pi_XR_X(s)=\pi_X$, $R_X(s)R_X(t)=R_X(s)$, and $\pi_ZR_X(s)=R_X(s)|_Z\pi_Z$ for $X<Z$ on overlaps. They are continuous on their stratified domains and smooth on individual strata. For a fixed reference $a\in(0,1)$, $(R_X(a),\rho_X)$ identifies the punctured tube with $S_X(a)\times(0,1)$, where $S_X(a)=W\cap\{\rho_X=a\}$; adjoining $X$ identifies it with the corresponding open mapping cylinder of $\pi_X:S_X(a)\to X$. This is a controlled topological collar; no semialgebraicity of the resulting flows is asserted.
items.strategy: Rescale each squared radius by a positive smooth function of the base point to normalize the tube domains, which preserves the control equations and local properness over compact slices ([[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]]). For each stratum $X$ construct a field lifting the radial target field $(0,r)$ on $W\cap T_X\setminus X$ by increasing dimension: use right inverses of $(d\pi_X,d\rho_X)$ on minimal strata and lift lower fields through intermediate controllers elsewhere; the active middle-band controllers form chains, so patching with a subordinate smooth partition preserves the linear control equations ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]; AC meets its countable-choice hypothesis via [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Integrability on all positive levels follows from a compact-trapping argument: near a lower stratum, a compact base slice with a closed radius band is invariant while the projected lower flow exists, and a finite maximal endpoint would have to approach a lower stratum with constant positive radius, which is impossible ([[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]). This produces the radial family satisfying the semigroup, projection and control equations. Commutation on incident overlaps is obtained by a decreasing-dimensional correction: conjugate the $X$ family by the already fixed $Y$ transports near the inner $Y$ band using a smooth radial reparametrisation, which is the identity near the outer boundary; the conjugation preserves all normalization, projection and control equations and commutes with $Y$ transports on the inner band. In the normalized coordinates the family identifies the punctured tube with $S_X(a)\times(0,1)$, and continuity at the adjoined zero end follows from the uniform normal-bundle estimates on compact slices.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for the partition-of-unity and ODE suppliers ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the inherited tube data come from the control-data lemma. No other choice principle is used.

John Mather, Notes on Topological Stability (1970), Sections 6-10 (tubular neighbourhoods, control data, controlled vector fields and parameter groups)

items.title: Finite simplicial maps have explicit compatible triangulated mapping cylinders
items.statement:
Let $f:K\to L$ be a simplicial map of finite complexes; vertex identifications are allowed. Its topological mapping cylinder
$$M_f=(|K|\times[0,1]\sqcup|L|)/((x,0)\sim f(x))$$
has a finite triangulation of dimension at most $\max(\dim K+1,\dim L)$ and a homeomorphism $H$ to $M_f$ fixing both boundary copies. The triangulated cylinder retraction to $|L|$ is piecewise linear. Before triangulating, its cells and $H$ have explicit formulas. For every finite collection of pairs of subcomplexes $(K_j,L_j)$ with $f(K_j)\subseteq L_j$, the corresponding cylinders are subpolyhedra; one simultaneous subdivision makes them subcomplexes. The construction also retains the top subpolyhedron $f^{-1}(|L_j|)$ for each $L_j$. On each cell away from the collapsed end, $H$ is smooth in affine coordinates; no immersion or smooth tangent-star claim is made at a collapsed end. All boundaries may be subdivided: the lemma does not promise an extension of an arbitrarily fixed boundary triangulation without subdivision.
items.strategy: Write $z_i=\sum_{f(v)=i}x_v$ and cut each source simplex by the hyperplanes $f_i=f_j$; the resulting finite polytopal cells carry the join cells $A*C$ for the maximal vertex sets $I(C)$, with the intersection identity $(A*C)\cap(A'*C')=(A\cap A')*(C\cap C')$. Triangulate the finite polytopal complex by coning each cell from an interior point over its already triangulated boundary; the dimension bound follows from the independence of the equal-maximum equations on each image simplex. The normalized fibre coordinates $P_i(x)_v=x_v/f_i(x)$ give the explicit homeomorphism $H$, bijectivity follows from the threshold equation $\sum_i\min(z_i,m)=t$ and its inverse formulas, and continuity at the collapsed end uses compactness of $|K|$ and closedness of the quotient map; the retraction is affine on join cells, hence PL. Subcomplex pairs and the top subpolyhedra are unions of cells, and one barycentric subdivision makes them full. All facts about realizations are from [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-weak-topology-agrees-with-euclidean-topology]] and [[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]].
items.axiom_use: None: finite polytopal constructions, finitely many cells and simplices.

references.title: R. M. Goresky, Triangulation of stratified objects, section 4 (triangulated mapping cylinders), printed pp. 197-199

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit compatible finite triangulations
items.statement: Assume AC. A compact finite controlled Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth ambient space admits a finite triangulation of dimension at most the largest real stratum dimension, compatible with every stratum closure and any prescribed union of strata. Each open stratum is a union of open simplices. The homeomorphism is smooth on the pieces within each stratum. The construction may make the finitely many normal link-bundle projections between triangulated compact stratum cores piecewise linear. It does not make an arbitrary algebraic map globally simplicial. In particular it applies individually to compactifications of quasi-projective complex varieties and to their compact controlled links, once the stated Whitney/control hypotheses have been supplied.
items.strategy: Use the normalized commuting radial collars of [[lem-compact-controlled-whitney-spaces-admit-commuting-radial-collars]]. For a stratum $X$ and level $a$, the closure of the level set meets only incident upper strata and lower frontier strata and is a compact controlled space of strictly smaller dimension; inherited projections are submersive on its strata, its cores (strata with lower tubes removed) are compact smooth manifolds with corners whose active radius functions have independent differentials, and the core-to-base maps are proper corner submersions with compatible faces ([[thm-constant-rank-theorem-for-manifolds]]; local constructions use [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]] and AC through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Flow the coordinate fields of the corner charts to obtain genuine finite smooth bundle product charts, supplying the hypotheses of the relative manifold and bundle triangulation suppliers [[thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations]], [[thm-smooth-bundles-admit-relative-finite-triangulations-over-a-fixed-base-triangulation]] and the projection-preserving fitting supplier [[lem-relative-smooth-triangulations-can-be-fitted-while-preserving-a-bundle-projection]]. Induct on dimension with partial triangulations $C_{(n,p)}$ of top boundaries controlled by $p$-dimensional lower strata and interior triangulations $B_n$, retaining buffers and using subcomplex-compatibility given by the radial collars; finally attach each stratum collar by the explicit mapping cylinder [[lem-finite-simplicial-maps-have-explicit-compatible-triangulated-mapping-cylinders]], whose endpoints and subcylinder behaviour match the marked level complexes. Finitely many $(n,p)$ assertions and finitely many parameter decreases leave a positive final radius.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for the partition-of-unity and ODE suppliers and the inherited collar construction ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The triangulation inductions are finite.

items.title: Finite simplicial open stars have explicit conical product charts
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\sigma$ be a nonempty simplex. Let $\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma$ be the subcomplex of simplices $\tau$ disjoint from $\sigma$ such that $\sigma\cup\tau\in K$. Define the open star to consist of points whose coordinates at every vertex of $\sigma$ are positive. Then
$$\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)\cong\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|),$$
where $c_{<1}(L)=(L\times[0,1))/(L\times\{0\})$ with the quotient topology, and the cone on the empty space means a single apex. The homeomorphism takes each simplex interior containing $\sigma$ to the product with the corresponding link-simplex interior and positive radial coordinate; the simplex $\sigma$ itself maps to the apex. The link is compact and has finitely many simplices. If $D\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma\notin D$, this star lies in $|K|\setminus|D|$.
items.strategy: Represent the truncated cone inside the link's coordinate space as $E=\{rq:0<r<1,\ q\in|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|\}\cup\{0\}$ and check that the quotient map is a homeomorphism at the apex using compactness of the link and product neighbourhoods. For a point $x$ of the star split its barycentric coordinates into the $\sigma$ part of total mass $a>0$ and the outside part $z$ of mass $r=1-a<1$; the normalized $\sigma$-coordinates times $(1-r)$ and the coordinates $z$ define mutually inverse continuous maps, and the outside support is a simplex of the link. The star is open by the finite positivity conditions, and no point of the star lies in $|D|$ when $\sigma\notin D$, since supports are closed under faces. All realization facts are from [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-weak-topology-agrees-with-euclidean-topology]] and [[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]].
items.axiom_use: None: explicit finite barycentric coordinate formulas and compactness of a finite realization.

references.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026; Section 2.1-2.3 (simplicial sheaves and star neighbourhoods)

items.title: Finite cell local system cohomology is finite and commutes with field extension
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,A)$ be a finite CW pair of dimension $d$, let $k$ be a field and let $L$ be a $k$-vector-space local system with finite-dimensional fibres. Then $H^q(X,A;L)$ is finite-dimensional, vanishes for $q<0$ and $q>d$, and for every field extension $k\subseteq k'$ the natural map is an isomorphism:
$$H^q(X,A;L)\otimes_k k'\cong H^q(X,A;L\otimes_k k').$$
The assertion holds separately on every component, including the empty pair.
items.strategy: By [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]] the groups are those of the cellular cochain complex, whose degree-$q$ term is a finite product of finite-dimensional fibres over finitely many relative $q$-cells for a finite CW pair, so it vanishes outside $[0,d]$ and has finite-dimensional kernels, images and cohomology ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]] for the transport data). The cellular differential is a finite sum of integer incidence coefficients times transport maps, and tensoring with $k'$ carries it to the differential for $L\otimes_kk'$, identifying the tensor of the complexes with the complex of the extended system. Tensoring a short exact sequence of $k$-vector spaces with the field extension preserves exactness, so cohomology commutes with $k\otimes_k-$ and the stated natural map is an isomorphism. AC is inherited exactly from the cellular-cochains supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); every sum and product here is finite.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed only because [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]] assumes it ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the finite-dimensional linear algebra and coefficient comparison are choice-free.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 3.H (local coefficients); cellular chains with local coefficients

items.title: Algebraically constructible sheaves have finite compatible stratified and local cochain models
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.
items.strategy: Choose a projective closure $\overline X$ of $X$ and apply the compatible Whitney stratification construction [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]] (including its upstream algebraic stratification input), also respecting the boundary $B=\overline X\setminus X$ and the closures of the marked supports and stratal pieces. Embed $\overline X^{\mathrm{an}}$ smoothly in Euclidean space by the Hermitian rank-one projector $z\mapsto zz^*/\|z\|^2$ and triangulate the resulting compact controlled Whitney space by [[lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations]], taking $D$ the subcomplex mapping onto $B$ and refining so all marked subsets are full subcomplexes; open simplices refine the complex strata and $\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$. On the retained simplices the finite-rank locally constant cohomology of $F$ lies in the essential image of the incidence model [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]], and the finite strict-face-chain bar resolutions [[lem-finite-poset-diagrams-have-bounded-finite-bar-models]] compute its ordinary and derived Hom with bounded finite-dimensional complexes. Compact-support and local statements use the open/closed support triangles of that model and the explicit finite star/cone models of [[lem-finite-simplicial-open-stars-have-explicit-conical-product-charts]]. Local constancy along a complex stratum follows from the conical chart $U\cong V\times cL$ of the neighbourhood theorem: on the contractible factor the pullback from the link is fully faithful, and the finite filtration of the link simplicial skeleta expresses the object by a finite coefficient complex. Field-extension compatibility reduces to the finite local-system comparison [[lem-finite-cell-local-system-cohomology-is-finite-and-commutes-with-field-extension]] and exactness of tensor product. AC is inherited exactly from the tube/partition and analytic derived-sheaf suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); all displayed matrix operations are finite.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through [[lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations]], [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; the final cochain computations are finite.

items.title: Complex algebraic constructible complexes have finite conical cochain models
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation. No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety, bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted to be a finite compact realization.
items.strategy: For each individual quasi-projective morphism and support collection, apply the compatible stratification theorem [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], the conical-neighbourhood theorem [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]] and the finite coiled-model theorem [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]; on the resulting finite deleted-boundary models the incidence theorem [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] proves the finite local and global cochain statements, internal-Hom constructibility and field-extension comparison, and choices for different operations need not form one jointly stratified cyclic diagram. A separated finite-type variety has a finite affine open cover with affine intersections (the diagonal is closed and each two-chart intersection is a closed subscheme of a product of affine charts, iterated); each intersection is quasi-projective, so the local construction applies, and the finite Cech derived augmentation of [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] assembles the local models into global finite bounded complexes, with uniformly bounded amplitudes and coefficient-extension compatibility. Compact-support models are assembled by the ordinary open/closed support triangles and internal Hom is locally computed on the finite affine cover with uniform bounds. AC is assumed and inherited from the geometric and analytic suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and inherited from [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]], [[lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations]] (through [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]), [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The assembly over a finite affine cover is finite.

items.title: A noncompact algebraic line needs a deleted boundary triangulation
items.statement: The analytic complex affine line $\mathbb A^1(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$ cannot be homeomorphic to the realization of a finite simplicial complex. It is homeomorphic to a finite triangulated compactification with one boundary vertex deleted. Thus "finite triangulation" for noncompact varieties must allow a deleted subcomplex or another equivalent noncompact finite-cell convention.
items.strategy: (1) The increasing open disks $\{|z|<n\}$ cover $\mathbb C$ but no finite subfamily does, so $\mathbb C$ is not compact; since finite simplicial realizations are compact ([[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]]), no finite realization is homeomorphic to $\mathbb C$. (2) The boundary complex $K$ of the octahedron realizes the $\ell^1$-sphere in $\mathbb R^3$; radial normalization and its inverse identify $|K|$ with $S^2$, and deleting the vertex $e_3$ gives $S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$. (3) The stereographic formula $(a,b)\mapsto(2a,2b,a^2+b^2-1)/(a^2+b^2+1)$ is a homeomorphism $\mathbb C\to S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$ with inverse $u\mapsto(u_1,u_2)/(1-u_3)$. Hence $\mathbb C$ is a finite complex with one vertex deleted, which is the compactification convention used by the finite triangulation statements on the companion page.
items.axiom_use: None: explicit formulas and the elementary noncompactness argument.
